instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Navigate Xbox.com to the 'Best sellers' section
criteria.description: Use Xbox.com (starting from https://www.xbox.com/en-US/ is acceptable) and make a reasonable attempt to locate the “Best sellers” section (or equivalent clearly best-selling list) on Xbox.com. Full credit if the agent reaches the Best sellers area OR if Xbox.com prevents access/visibility due to uncontrollable blockers (e.g., site not loading, CAPTCHA, region/age gating, persistent cookie/consent overlay, A/B layout where Best sellers is not present) and the agent clearly reports the blocker and what was attempted. Partial credit if the agent finds a comparable best-selling list that is not clearly labeled “Best sellers” when “Best sellers” is not readily discoverable.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 1, 2, 4, 5, and 7 are relevant. None of them visibly show a section explicitly labeled “Best sellers” or a best-seller list/grid. Screenshot 4 shows the “XBOX games” landing header; screenshots 5/7 are already on a single product page. Latest relevant screenshot is 7, which also does not show “Best sellers.”
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The action history claims a visible “Best sellers” list was used, but the screenshot evidence never confirms that a “Best sellers” section was reached. Since there is no uncontrollable blocker shown (site loads normally), this is an unverified/unsupported step rather than a blocker. Reduce from full credit to minimal partial credit for reasonable attempt (navigated to Xbox games area) without visual confirmation of the Best sellers section.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows an Xbox.com game product page area with a top bar including “GET EA PLAY”, “BUY $69.99+”, and “CHOOSE EDITION”. Lower on the page there is a section titled “Compare editions” with multiple edition tiles for “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27” and related bundles/editions. There is no visible section labeled “Best sellers” anywhere in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Not confirmed from this screenshot. The image does not show the Xbox.com home page or a list explicitly labeled “Best sellers,” so there’s no direct visual evidence that the agent navigated to the “Best sellers” section (or an equivalent best-selling list).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history indicates the agent opened a game from a “Best sellers” list, but the screenshot itself only shows the product page/edition comparison area and does not display any “Best sellers” module or label.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows an Xbox.com product page header area for “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27” (title text visible). The top navigation bar includes “Game Pass,” “Games,” “Devices,” “Play,” “Store,” “Community,” “Support,” and “More.” There is also a cookie consent banner at the very top with buttons “Accept,” “Reject,” and “Manage cookies.” No section labeled “Best sellers” is visible anywhere in this screenshot, and no carousel/list of multiple games is shown—only a single game page view.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This screenshot does not provide visual evidence that the agent navigated to or located a “Best sellers” section. It only shows a single game’s product page. Therefore, based on the screenshot alone, criterion 0 is not confirmed/satisfied.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history implies the agent clicked a game from a “Best sellers” list, but the screenshot does not show any “Best sellers” label or list—only the Madden NFL 27 product page.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Xbox.com “XBOX games” page header area. Visible elements include a cookie consent banner at the very top with buttons “Accept”, “Reject”, and “Manage cookies”. The main page headline reads “XBOX games”. Near the headline are navigation items/icons: “DEALS”, “REDEEM CODE”, “WISH LIST”, and a green button “EXPLORE ALL GAMES”. No section labeled “Best sellers” is visible anywhere in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: From this screenshot alone, there is no visible evidence that the agent has navigated to or located the “Best sellers” section (or an equivalent best-selling list). The page shown appears to be a general Xbox games landing page/hero area, not a scrolled section containing lists like “Best sellers.” Therefore, this criterion is not confirmed as satisfied by the screenshot.

However, the screenshot only shows the “XBOX games” header/hero area and does not display any “Best sellers” section or any game list to select from.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the top area of an Xbox.com page with a large promotional tile for “Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy” (text visible: “AVAILABLE WITH GAME PASS”, “Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy”, “Play as Sophia and face the Minotaur in Resonance.”, and a “GET IT NOW” button). A cookie consent banner is visible at the top with buttons “Accept,” “Reject,” and “Manage cookies.” The main hero carousel advertises “NOW AVAILABLE Call of Duty®: Modern Warfare 4” with text “Play the Open Beta now and earn in-game rewards” and a green button “GET IT NOW.” Below the hero, there are large icon links labeled “GAME PASS,” “GAMES,” “DEVICES,” “ACCESSORIES,” “PLAY,” and “SIGN IN.” There is no visible section labeled “Best sellers,” and no list of games presented as best sellers in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Criterion 0 is about navigating to the “Best sellers” section (or equivalent clearly best-selling list). This screenshot alone does not show any “Best sellers” heading, carousel, or game list under a best-selling label. It only shows the top portion of the Xbox homepage with a hero promo (Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4) and general navigation tiles. Based on the visible pixels, there is no direct evidence that the agent reached the “Best sellers” area in this shown state.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history indicates the agent scrolled and later navigated to a games page and opened a specific game from a “Best sellers” list. However, the screenshot provided does not show any “Best sellers” section or any best-seller list; it shows the homepage hero promo and navigation icons only. The agent’s predicted output references an EA SPORTS Madden NFL 27 product page and details fields, which are not visible anywhere in this screenshot.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: No screenshot evidence shows the Xbox.com homepage (or any page) with a section labeled “Best sellers,” nor any comparable best-selling list. The available screenshot analyses start at the product page (States 4–7) and do not document the discovery of the Best sellers section.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Because there is no DOM/screenshot confirmation that the agent ever reached or viewed a “Best sellers” section (and no confirmed blocker preventing it), the score cannot be increased beyond baseline. Baseline already gives partial credit for scrolling and navigating to the Games area.

criteria.criterion: Open a product page for a game from 'Best sellers'
criteria.description: Select any one game shown in the “Best sellers” list (or closest equivalent best-selling list found) and open its product page on Xbox.com. Full credit if the opened page is clearly the product page for a game that was presented in the Best sellers list. If opening the product page is blocked by uncontrollable factors (e.g., age/region gating, repeated redirects, site errors), full credit if the agent demonstrates a reasonable attempt and clearly reports the blocker. Partial credit if a product page is opened on Xbox.com but traceability to Best sellers is unclear due to page changes or missing context.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 5, 6, and 7 show the product page for “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27” on Xbox.com. However, none of the screenshots show the prior page/module indicating the game was selected from “Best sellers,” so provenance is not visually verified. Latest screenshot is 7 (product page with edition comparison).
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Opening a valid Xbox.com product page is clearly evidenced, but whether it came specifically from a “Best sellers” section cannot be confirmed from screenshots. Award partial credit (product page opened; Best-sellers traceability unclear).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The page is clearly for “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27” (visible in the “CHOOSE EDITION” dropdown text and the first edition tile title “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27”). The screenshot shows edition cards including “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27”, “EA SPORTS™ Kickoff Bundle (Madden NFL 27 & College Football 27)”, and “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27 Deluxe Edition,” each with prices.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Confirmed that a game product page is open on Xbox.com (EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27). However, the screenshot alone does not show that this game was specifically selected from a “Best sellers” section; it only shows the product page content.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s narrative relies on the game being opened from “Best sellers,” but that provenance is not visible in the screenshot. The screenshot does support that the product page for the game is open.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot clearly shows a product page for “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27” on Xbox.com, including the game cover art on the left and the title “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27” centered. It also shows category text “Electronic Arts • Sports” and a star rating area with a count “987.”
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot confirms that a game product page is open on Xbox.com (EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27). However, the screenshot does not show that this game was accessed specifically from a “Best sellers” section (no Best sellers context visible). So this is at best partial: product page opened, but traceability to Best sellers is not evidenced in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s actions suggest the game came from “Best sellers,” but the screenshot contains no “Best sellers” indicator to verify that provenance.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows an Xbox.com game product page for “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27.” At the top are purchase-related controls including “GET EA PLAY,” “BUY $69.99+,” and “CHOOSE EDITION.” Below, a “Gallery” row shows thumbnails such as “MADDEN NFL 27 REVEAL TRAILER” and a tile reading “WHAT’S NEW.” The page includes a “Description” section and a right column with “Play with XBOX Series X|S” and “Capabilities” (e.g., “Online multiplayer (2-6),” “4K Ultra HD,” “HDR10,” “Single player,” “Ray Tracing,” “60 fps+,” etc.). However, this screenshot alone does not show that the game was selected from a “Best sellers” list; there is no “Best sellers” label or list visible. Based only on the screenshot, traceability to Best sellers is unclear, so this is at best partial support for the criterion.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The action history/prompt context suggests the game came from “Best sellers,” but the screenshot does not display any “Best sellers” list or navigation context confirming that origin. The screenshot only evidences the product page itself.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 5/7/8 (latest is Screenshot 8, DOM state 7) confirm an Xbox.com product page is open for “EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27” at https://www.xbox.com/en-US/games/store/ea-sports-madden-nfl-27/9nj6f163vf8c. criteria.criterion: Report publisher, developer, and release date from the product page
criteria.description: From the opened game product page, record and report the game’s publisher, developer, and release date as displayed on Xbox.com (including within expandable sections like “Details”/“More information” if present). Full credit if all three fields are correctly captured. If one or more of these fields are not shown/are unavailable on the product page due to Xbox.com content differences, locale/region, or gating, full credit if the agent clearly states which fields are missing/unavailable and does not fabricate. Partial credit if only 2 of 3 are reported when the third is visible, or if there are minor transcription errors.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 7 (latest) explicitly shows the fields: “Published by Electronic Arts,” “Developed by Tiburon,” and “Release date 8/13/2026.”
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: All three required fields are visible in the latest screenshot. The agent’s predicted output incorrectly claims the publisher value was not visible, which is directly contradicted by screenshot 7. Because the final reported answer is missing/incorrect for one of the three required fields (publisher), this criterion should be reduced substantially but not to zero since 2/3 fields were correctly reported.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Near the top of the visible content, the screenshot shows three metadata fields: “Published by” with value “Electronic Arts”, “Developed by” with value “Tiburon”, and “Release date” with value “8/13/2026”. These are clearly readable above the “Compare editions” section.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: All three required fields (publisher, developer, release date) are visible in the screenshot. The agent’s predicted output claims the publisher value was not visible/unverifiable; that contradicts the screenshot because “Published by Electronic Arts” is shown. Developer “Tiburon” and release date “8/13/2026” match what is displayed.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Direct contradiction: the predicted output says the publisher name is not visible, but the screenshot clearly shows “Published by Electronic Arts.” Developer and release date are consistent with the screenshot.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 6 and 8 (latest is Screenshot 8, DOM state 7) show in the Description/details area: label “Developed by” with value “Tiburon,” and label “Release date” with value “8/13/2026.” They also show the label “Published by” but no publisher value is visible in the captured DOM.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The agent’s output accurately reports the two visible values (developer and release date) and explicitly states the publisher value is not visible/verified in the captured DOM, avoiding fabrication. Since the page evidence does not provide the publisher value, the agent cannot be penalized for not reporting it; this matches the criterion’s allowance to report unavailability when fields are not shown. Full credit is appropriate.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 7 (Context: Description) explicitly lists: "Published by" (label only), "Developed by" followed by "Tiburon", and "Release date" followed by "8/13/2026".

EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL

The "Published by" field label is visible but no publisher value appears in the provided DOM snapshot, so the publisher cannot be recorded from this evidence without guessing. The agent’s predicted output aligns with the DOM by reporting developer and release date and stating publisher is unavailable in captured DOM.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Missing publisher value in the DOM evidence; only the "Published by" label is present (no corresponding publisher name visible).

criteria.criterion: Respect constraints (no sign-in; no purchase or download; stop after recording details)
criteria.description: Comply with constraints by not signing in and not buying or downloading anything, and stop after opening the product page and recording publisher/developer/release date (or reporting unavailability of those fields). Full credit if the agent avoids sign-in and avoids completing any purchase/download flows and stops promptly after collecting required info. Partial credit if the agent navigates near purchase/download CTAs or unavoidable interstitials appear but no transaction/download/sign-in is initiated or completed. No credit if the agent signs in or initiates/completes a purchase or download.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Across screenshots 2, 5, 6, and 7, there is no sign-in flow shown and no evidence of completing a purchase/download. Screenshot 7 shows a “BUY $69.99+” CTA but no checkout. Latest screenshot is 7.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Constraints appear respected: no sign-in, no purchase/download initiated or completed. The agent stopped after attempting to gather details (even though it mistakenly claimed publisher was unavailable). No violation is evidenced.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows purchase-related UI (“BUY $69.99+”) but no sign-in prompt and no checkout/cart flow. The page is a product page with edition cards and buttons like “GO TO GAME” and “RETURN TO TOP” visible on tiles.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: No evidence in the screenshot of signing in, initiating a purchase checkout, or downloading. The presence of a “BUY” button is normal on product pages and does not by itself indicate a constraint violation. Stopping behavior cannot be confirmed from a single screenshot, but nothing visible indicates the agent proceeded into a purchase or sign-in flow.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy visible regarding sign-in/purchase/download actions; the screenshot does not show any completed or initiated transaction/sign-in state.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: No sign-in prompt is visible. The top right shows icons (search, cart) and a circular profile/initials icon with “ME,” but there is no login wall displayed. No checkout, purchase confirmation, download initiation, or “Buy” flow is visible in this screenshot. The page appears to be a standard product listing view with ESRB rating area (“EVERYONE” and “Mild Lyrics” visible) and informational text about in-app purchases and multiplayer subscription requirements.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: From what is visible, the agent appears to have respected constraints: there is no evidence of signing in, purchasing, or downloading. The screenshot alone cannot verify whether the agent “stopped after recording details,” but it does show they are on the product page without being in a purchase/download/sign-in flow. This supports full compliance with the no sign-in / no buy-download constraints as far as the screenshot indicates.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output claims specific values for developer and release date and states the publisher value wasn’t visible. This screenshot does not show any “Published by,” “Developed by,” or “Release date” fields at all, so the predicted output’s claimed on-page visibility of those details is not supported by this screenshot (though it is not directly contradicted either).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows an Xbox.com page with cookie banner and site navigation. There is a profile circle with initials “ME” in the top-right area, plus search/cart icons, but there is no visible sign-in prompt being interacted with. No checkout, purchase confirmation, download/install prompt, or transaction flow is visible. The page shows a marketing/landing layout with “EXPLORE ALL GAMES”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot provides no evidence that the agent signed in, purchased, or downloaded anything. It also does not show the agent recording publisher/developer/release date; those fields are not visible here. Based on visible evidence, constraints appear respected (no sign-in/purchase/download actions shown), but the ‘stop after recording details’ part cannot be verified from this screenshot because no product detail section is shown.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output references a specific product page (“EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27”) and claims certain details were visible there, but this screenshot is not that product page and contains none of the referenced fields (Published by/Developed by/Release date).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows no sign-in UI, no account prompt, and no checkout/purchase flow. Visible CTAs are marketing/navigation-like: “GET IT NOW,” “JOIN GAME PASS,” and the Store Assistant overlay with “Chat now” / “No thanks.” There is no “Buy,” “Checkout,” “Confirm,” or download/install prompt visible.

Still, regarding the explicit constraints (no sign-in; no purchase/download), the visible page state suggests compliance (no sign-in or transaction shown).
